# Experimental Results

## Overview

This document explains the outputs generated by the RRAI Refactoring
Verification Framework.

After executing

```bash
python src/main.py
```

or

```bash
python examples/complete_demo.py
```

all experimental results are written to the `results/` directory.

---

# Generated Files

The framework produces four output files.

```
results/

proof_obligations.csv
behavioural_results.csv
scalability_results.csv
divergence_positions.png
```

---

# proof_obligations.csv

This file summarizes theorem verification results.

Each row corresponds to one refactoring theorem.

Typical contents include

| Transformation | Result |
|----------------|--------|
| Decomposition | PASS |
| Merging | PASS |
| Elimination | PASS |
| Priority Adjustment | PASS |
| Invalid Merge | FAIL |
| Invalid Priority Adjustment | FAIL |
| Unsafe Decomposition | FAIL |

A PASS result indicates that all proof obligations were satisfied.

A FAIL result indicates that at least one proof obligation was violated.

---

# behavioural_results.csv

This file summarizes execution-based behavioural validation.

Each row contains

- transformation name;
- number of executions;
- number of behavioural divergences;
- divergence percentage.

Example

| Transformation | Executions | Divergences | Divergence (%) |
|---------------|-----------:|------------:|---------------:|
| Decomposition | 10000 | 0 | 0.00 |
| Merging | 10000 | 0 | 0.00 |
| Elimination | 10000 | 0 | 0.00 |
| Priority Adjustment | 10000 | 0 | 0.00 |
| Invalid Merge | 10000 | 2466 | 24.66 |
| Invalid Priority Adjustment | 10000 | 3081 | 30.81 |
| Unsafe Decomposition | 10000 | 4929 | 49.29 |

Behavioural divergence represents executions for which the transformed
rule base no longer behaves equivalently to the original system.

---

# scalability_results.csv

This file reports the execution time of behavioural validation.

Each row contains

- number of traces;
- average execution time;
- standard deviation (if available).

Example

| Traces | Mean Time (s) |
|--------:|--------------:|
| 100 | 0.083 |
| 500 | 0.452 |
| 1000 | 0.902 |
| 2000 | 1.796 |
| 5000 | 4.584 |
| 10000 | 9.182 |

These measurements demonstrate the scalability of the proposed
verification framework.

---

# divergence_positions.png

This figure visualizes where behavioural divergence first occurs during
execution.

The x-axis represents the execution step at which the first mismatch is
detected.

The y-axis represents the number of executions whose first divergence
appears at that step.

Only incorrect refactorings generate divergence data.

Correctness-preserving transformations should produce no divergence.

---

# Interpreting the Results

The framework combines two complementary forms of verification.

## Formal Verification

The proof obligation results establish that the structural conditions
required by each refactoring theorem are satisfied.

These checks are deterministic.

---

## Behavioural Validation

Execution-based validation confirms that the transformed rule base
produces behaviour equivalent to the original system.

Repeated Monte Carlo execution provides empirical evidence supporting
the formal verification results.

---

## Scalability Evaluation

The scalability experiment measures the computational cost of behavioural
validation.

Increasing execution time with larger workloads is expected.

The reported measurements demonstrate that the framework remains
practical for thousands of execution traces.

---

# Expected Outcome

A successful execution of the framework should satisfy the following
conditions.

- All correctness-preserving refactorings pass theorem verification.
- All correctness-preserving refactorings produce zero behavioural
  divergence.
- All negative-control refactorings fail theorem verification.
- All negative-control refactorings produce observable behavioural
  divergence.
- The generated reports are written successfully to the `results/`
  directory.

Together, these outputs provide both formal and empirical evidence for
the correctness-preserving rule refactorings implemented in the
framework.
